Summary

## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Requests using provider-qualified model entries now retain supported tools and tool choices, rather than relying on a less-specific model entry. * If no provider-specific entry is available, compatibility checks fall back to the general model entry and continue to omit unsupported tools. * Provider-specific compatibility information is also used when determining whether chat requests with reasoning and tools should be routed through the Responses API. Compat now selects supported parameters using the request provider and model. It prefers a provider-qualified catalog entry and falls back to the existing model lookup. Parameter filtering and the reasoning-with-tools routing check use this lookup. **Changes: Compat parameter lookup** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Provider-aware lookup and parameter filtering**
`plugins/compat/main.go`, `plugins/compat/hooks_test.go`|The lookup prefers a provider-qualified parameter list and falls back to the bare model entry when no qualified entry exists. Parameter filtering and the reasoning-with-tools routing check use the provider-aware lookup. Tests cover qualified-row precedence and bare-row fallback.| **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium **Suggested reviewers:** `sammaji`
Merge Risk: Low · up to e0dac

Compat now prefers the provider-qualified model-parameters row, so tools and tool_choice are kept when a bare row conflicts. The change is low risk. Before merge, add the repository-required provider-harness coverage for the changed request behavior, or point to the upstack PR that supplies it.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title "[fix]: compat - prefer the provider-qualified model-parameters row" names the main change: the compat plugin now looks up the provider-qualified catalog row before the bare model key. It matches the code change in plugins/compat/main.go and the regression test. The title is specific and concise, and it follows the repository's bracketed-prefix style.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description fills most of the template. It has a clear Summary that explains the bug (OpenRouter GPT-6 Luna losing tools and tool_choice), a Changes section with design notes and a stated trade-off, the Type of change (Bug fix), Affected areas (Plugins), a How to test section with commands and the new test's expected behavior, a Breaking changes answer, and Related issues (Closes `#9356`). Security considerations is filled in. Gaps: the Checklist is absent, and the Screenshots section is not addressed (it is optional for non-UI changes). The top-level sections are complete enough to review.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** Compared with the merge base, the PR changes plugins/compat/main.go and plugins/compat/hooks_test.go only. The main.go changes add supportedParametersFor, rename the local variable provider to reqProvider in PreLLMHook, and switch two call sites to the new helper. The test change adds TestDropParamsPrefersProviderQualifiedRow. All of these changes serve issue `#9356`, either by implementing provider-qualified preference or by testing it. No unrelated file or behavior change appears. The incomplete fallback behavior is a gap in requirement coverage, and it is assessed under linkedIssuesAssessment, not here.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#9356`] Provider-qualified preference is implemented. In plugins/compat/main.go, supportedParametersFor(provider, model) looks up <provider>/<model> first. The param-drop path in PreLLMHook and markReasoningWithToolsForResponses both call it. For openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna, the OpenRouter chat row is selected when both rows exist. The new test TestDropParamsPrefersProviderQualifiedRow covers this for Chat Completions only. [`#9356`] Requirement 2 is not met. The issue requires that an unqualified fallback row match the request provider and fit the request mode or endpoints, so that a Decisions-only row does not govern chat or Responses parameters. The bare-key fallback in supportedParametersFor is unconditional, and it still calls supportedParameters(provider, model) without any provider or mode check. The second case of the new test asserts that a bare Decisions-only openai/gpt-6-luna row drops tools for an OpenRouter request. This is the regression case the issue names as required, and it is not implemented. The PR description states this limitation. [`#9356`] Suggested coverage is incomplete. The diff adds no Responses-endpoint test, no native Decisions request test, and no unknown-model test. **Resolution** In supportedParametersFor, use the bare-key row only when its provider matches the request provider and its mode or supported endpoints fit the request type (chat or Responses). Otherwise return nil so that no allowlist applies. This requires the parameters index to expose each row's provider and mode or endpoints. Because the plugin pins a released framework, the framework change may need to land first. Invert the second test case so that a Decisions-only bare row does not drop tools for an OpenRouter request. Add tests for the Responses endpoint, native Decisions requests, and unknown-model behavior.
